steps.description: Reframe the Algebraic Independence Hypothesis as a symbolic polynomial identity testing problem. Given a set of functions $F = \{f_1, \dots, f_m\}$ (e.g., $\{1, x, x^2, \sin(2\pi x)\}$), determine if there exists a non-zero polynomial $P \in \mathbb{Q}[y_1, \dots, y_m]$ such that $P(f_1(x), \dots, f_m(x)) \equiv 0$ for all $x$. Use symbolic algebra tools (SymPy or Lean) to construct a candidate polynomial relation via Gröbner basis elimination or random evaluation testing. If no non-trivial relation is found within degree $d$, conclude algebraic independence over $\mathbb{Q}$.
